accuracy.evidence: Checked a² − b² = (a+b)(a−b) against CCSS A-SSE.2 and GCSE Algebra factorisation. Hand checks: x²−49=(x+7)(x−7); 9x²−25=(3x+5)(3x−5); 4x²−81; 16y²−25; x²+49 rejected as a sum.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets (a−b)² for a²−b²; treating sums as differences; √(9x²)=9x; dropping a bracket. Lab reject step and challenge name each.

lab_distinct.evidence: flaga2b2 is algebraic factorising with coefficient roots and sum rejection. flagsqr is the geometric area / cutting demo for perfect squares. Under 30% overlap expected.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner reveals the identity, marks both brackets for x²−49, factorises 9x²−25, rejects x²+49, and orders squares-then-minus method.

predictions.evidence: Tempting wrongs: (a−b)²; (x−7)²; (9x+5)(x−5); claiming +49 still works; ignoring the sign.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Tags sq/coef/sum/miss/true explain (a−b)² expansion, coefficient roots, and why plus blocks the pattern.

readability.evidence: Curriculum terms: difference of two squares, factorise, perfect square, coefficient, expand. Short sentences.

no_filler.evidence: No filler phrases. Each paragraph teaches identity, example, coefficients, or rejection.

mobile.evidence: Bracket tiles and option rows sized for phone; button twins for each mark.

accessibility.evidence: Buttons for every tile/tap; aria-label live; axe AA via walk.cjs.

sources: CCSS Math A-SSE.2 — use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it
AQA GCSE Mathematics — factorising the difference of two squares
